default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1358.title: Mean-median skew cross
E-1358.hypothesis: When the rolling mean of closes moves above the rolling median while price is above the mean, recent prices are pulling the distribution up: a late trend of buyers lifting offers; follow.

E-1359.title: Relative cumulative volume break
E-1359.hypothesis: A session whose cumulative volume runs ahead of its usual pace has participants with size; a break of the recent range on the day's side of the open continues as they keep working orders.

E-1360.title: Semivariance imbalance follow
E-1360.hypothesis: When nearly all recent squared returns come from up bars (or down bars), the move is one-sided pressure rather than noise; follow the dominant side.

E-1361.title: Time spent in the upper half of the range
E-1361.hypothesis: Closing in the upper (lower) half of the rolling range for most of the window shows persistent acceptance of higher (lower) prices; follow when the share crosses the threshold.

E-1362.title: Volume-confirmed return follow
E-1362.hypothesis: When bar returns correlate positively with volume in a window that is net up (down), size is pushing price rather than absorbing it; follow.

E-1363.title: Clock-relative dead tape break
E-1363.hypothesis: A window much quieter than the same clock time usually is, followed by a close beyond its range, means liquidity providers stepped away and a directional order is moving a thin book; follow.

E-1364.title: Low bar-overlap trend
E-1364.hypothesis: Consecutive bars that barely overlap mean price is travelling without two-way trade; one-sided auction continues in the direction of the net move.

E-1365.title: Whipsaw-regime edge fade
E-1365.hypothesis: When intrabar ranges are large relative to close-to-close changes (Parkinson/close-vol ratio), price is whipsawing; a close at the window's extreme is likely to revert.

E-1366.title: Session peak-volume bar level
E-1366.hypothesis: The bar with the most volume so far in the session marks where the most size changed hands; a close away from its midpoint shows which side lost, and price follows that side.

E-1367.title: Doji pause continuation
E-1367.hypothesis: After a larger-than-usual move, a doji bar is a pause by profit-takers; a close beyond the doji in the direction of the move signals the trend resuming.
